Misc. 781/40.
Bubbling Well Station.
December 8, 1940.
Japanese Military Barricades in the Western
District.
------------------------------------
On 8-12-40, there was no improvement in the situation
on the Barricaded Western Area roads.
In the forenoon, only two Buses of the Western
District Citizens Bus Company were operating, one on
each Route, and it was discovered that the third Bus
had broken down and was undergoing repairs on Kinnear
Road.
The repairs were however completed and the third
Bus was again brought into service at about 12 noon
8-12-40.
It was also noticed that these three Buses are
now operating without S.M.C. or C.M.F. number plates but
they are still use Chinese plates Nos. 5830, 5831 and
5832.
At 7 a.m. 8-12-40, the Shanghai General Omnibus
Company again commenced operating a single No. 1 Route
Bus between St. George's and Jessfield Park, via Jessfield
Kinnear, Edinburgh and Yu Yuen Roads and it was proposed
to run additional Buses on the same Route later in the
day.
However, at about 10.10 a.m. 8-12-40, members of
the S.C.G.P. Bureau from 13 Jessfield Road erected knife-
Rest Barricades on Kinnear Road, a few yards west of
Jessfield Road, and permitted the Bus, which was returning
to St. George's to pass through the Barricade to Jessfield
Road. The driver and Conductor were at the same time
informed by the S.C.G.Police that the Bus would not be
permitted to return again via Kinnear Road.
pages.zh:
杂项卷宗 781/40。
静安寺捕房。
1940年12月8日。
西区日军路障。
------------------------------------
1940年12月8日，封锁西区道路的状况未见改善。
上午，仅有两辆西区市民公共汽车公司的巴士在运营，每条路线各一辆，经查发现第三辆巴士发生故障，正在金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）进行维修。
维修工作随后完成，该第三辆巴士于1940年12月8日中午12时左右重新投入服务。
另注意到，这三辆巴士目前未悬挂工部局或法公董局的车牌，但仍使用中国车牌，号码分别为5830、5831和5832。
1940年12月8日上午7时，上海通用公共汽车公司再次开始运营一辆1路巴士，往返于圣乔治大厦与兆丰公园之间，途经兆丰路、金尼尔路、爱丁堡路及愚园路，并计划于当日稍后时间在该路线增派巴士。
然而，1940年12月8日上午10时10分左右，来自兆丰路13号的上海市警察局警员在金尼尔路上、距兆丰路西数码处设置了刀刺路障，并允许正返回圣乔治大厦的巴士穿过路障驶入兆丰路。与此同时，上海市警察告知司机和售票员，该巴士将不被允许再次经由金尼尔路返回。

pages.en:
- 2 -

At the same time a large number of S.C.G. Police,
armed with rifles, and bayonets, with higher officials in
attendance, were lined at intervals along Kinnear and
Jessfield Roads.

All pedestrians and traffic was however permitted to
pass through this Barricade without hinderance.

The undersigned and S/Inspector Li Shu Fa visited
13 Jessfield Road and ascertained that this was only a
temporary precaution owing to the Fact that the Mayor of
the Shanghai City Government was paying a visit to an
address on Kinnear Road.

The visit concluded, the party of S.C.G. Police
returned to 13 Jessfield Road at 11 a.m. leaving four
members to guard the Barricade which was partly opened
for traffic, but not removed. At 11.15 a.m. 8-12-40, the
undersigned informed a Foreign Inspector of the S.G.O. Co.
that the precautions had finished and they could resume
running the Bus via Kinnear Road.

When they did so however, the Bus was stopped at the
Kinnear Road Barricade, by the S.C.G. Police and turned
back without any explanation.

The undersigned and S/Inspector Li Shu Fa again
visited 13 Jessfield Road at 12 noon 8-12-40, but the
Inspector on duty stated he did not know on whose orders
the Bus was being prevented from proceeding via Kinnear
Road, but promised to find out and give his answer at 2 p.m.
8-12-40.

In the meantime however it was ascertained from the
S.C.G. Police Constables on duty at the Barricade that
they had received orders from the Japanese Gendarme to
prevent the Bus from proceeding via Kinnear Road.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

与此同时，大批配备步枪和刺刀的上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.C.G. Police）警员，在高级官员的督率下，沿金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）和极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）间隔列队布防。

然而，所有行人及车辆均获准无障碍通过此路障。

本人与李树发巡官（S/Inspector Li Shu Fa）前往极司菲尔路13号查访，获悉此举仅为临时预防措施，缘由是上海市政府市长正前往金尼尔路某址访问。

访问结束后，上海公共租界工部局警务处警队于上午11时返回极司菲尔路13号，留下四名警员看守路障；该路障已部分开放以通行车辆，但并未撤除。1940年12月8日上午11时15分，本人通知上海煤气公司（S.G.O. Co.）的一名外籍督察，称预防措施已结束，该公司可恢复经金尼尔路运营巴士。

然而，当该公司照办时，巴士却在金尼尔路路障处被上海公共租界工部局警务处警员拦停，并在未作任何解释的情况下被折返。

1940年12月8日中午12时，本人与李树发巡官再次前往极司菲尔路13号，但值班督察表示，他不知晓是谁下令阻止巴士经金尼尔路通行，但承诺查明情况，并于1940年12月8日下午2时给予答复。

与此同时，经向路障处执勤的上海公共租界工部局警务处警员了解，获悉他们已接到日本宪兵的命令，禁止巴士经金尼尔路通行。

pages.en:
- 3 -

The Shanghai General Omnibus Company were advised,
by Police, to run this particular Bus via Jessfield Road
and Brenan Road to Jessfield Park, but they replied that
the road surface was too bad and decided to return the
bus to the garage.

The same company are however, maintaining two Buses
on the No. 2 route, via Avenue Haig, Edinburgh, Gt. Western
and Columbia Roads to Amherst Avenue, as compared with
one Bus operating over the same route on 7-10-40.

Position of barricades and regulations pertaining
to same remained unchanged, but Foreigners are permitted
to pass in or out of the Blocked Area, through the
Barricades at bus stops, if they purchase a ticket for
the Western District Citizens Bus Company vehicles.

Certified true copy

pages.zh:
- 3 -

警方建议上海公共汽车公司（Shanghai General Omnibus Company）安排该特定班次公共汽车经极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）和布伦南路（Brenan Road）行驶至兆丰公园（Jessfield Park），但该公司回复称路面状况过于恶劣，并决定将该公共汽车返回车场。

然而，该公司在2路路线上仍维持两辆公共汽车的运营，路线经海格路（Avenue Haig）、爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）、大西路（Great Western Road）和哥伦比亚路（Columbia Road）至安赫斯特路（Amherst Avenue），而1940年10月7日在同一路线上运营的公共汽车仅为一辆。

路障的位置及相关规定保持不变，但外国人若购买西区市民公共汽车公司（Western District Citizens Bus Company）车辆的客票，则允许通过位于公共汽车站的路障进出封锁区。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
MSC File No. 281/40
B' ell. Station,
REPORT
Date. 8.12.40
19

Subject S. M. P. Policeman Injured.

Made by J. A. Walker. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that at 5 p.m. while proceeding
south along Edinburgh Road north of Kinnear Road I
noticed what appeared to be a person lying on the
corner of the road. I was riding a bicycle, which I
brought to a stop, and dismounted to investigate.

I then saw that the person was a S.M.P. Policeman
in uniform and that he had been severely injured
about the head.

There was a large quantity of blood on the road
which ran to the east gutter while the man's head,
which rested on his left arm, was also blood coated,
the man had the appearance of having lay there for
some time as part of the blood had clotted onto his
uniform.

I at once returned to Kinnear Road corner and
called the Kinnear Road patrol A.C.P.S.1088 in
charge.

Calling the patrol and the roadside traffic police
man I returned to the injured man and explained how I
had found him.

Several S.M.P. Police then arrived on the scene
and telephoned for an ambulance which they were un-
able to get. I then ordered C.P.C.390 to proceed to
Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads to call an ambulance
through the station which ambulance arrived about 7
minutes later and the injured man was removed to a
hospital.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
MSC 档案编号 281/40
白尔路捕房，
报告
日期：1940年12月8日
19

事由：上海公共租界工部局警务处警员受伤。

报告人：J. A. Walker。呈报人：[签名]

先生：

谨此报告，下午5时，当我沿金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）以北的爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）向南行进时，注意到路边角落似乎躺着一个人。我当时正骑着自行车，便停车下来查看。

随后我发现此人是一名身着制服的上海公共租界工部局警务处警员，其头部受重伤。

路面上有大量血迹，流向东侧的路边沟渠；该男子的头枕在左臂上，也沾满了血液。从部分血液已凝固在其制服上的情况来看，此人似乎已在此躺了一段时间。

我立即返回金尼尔路路口，呼叫负责该路段巡逻的助理巡长（A.C.P.S.）1088号。

叫来巡逻警员及路边交通警员后，我回到受伤者身边，说明了我发现他的经过。

随后几名上海公共租界工部局警务处警员抵达现场，并打电话呼叫救护车，但未能叫到。于是我命令中央公园捕房（C.P.C.）390号警员前往豫园路（Yu Yuen Road）与爱丁堡路路口，通过捕房呼叫救护车。救护车约7分钟后抵达，伤者随即被送往医院。

Bubbling Well Station,
December 6th, 1940.

Japanese Military Barricades in the Western District

The situation in the Blockaded Area on the
Western District Roads remained unchanged on 6/12/40.
The 3 M/Buses of the Western Shanghai Citizens
Bus Company commenced operating on the same Routes
as the previous day at 7a.m. 6/12/40, and no
additional Buses have been put into operation.
Foreigners however were refused permission to
pass the Barricades at East End of Yu Yuen Road and
Avenue Haig, even though they stated their intention
of proceeding by these Buses.
Police patrols were permitted to proceed west
on Great Western Road and through the Barricade at
Great Western - Edinburgh corner but not permitted
to return through the barricade in the opposite
direction.
Chinese in private m/cars and Silver Taxis
were permitted freely through this particular
Barricade after searching, but Foreigners on foot
or in m/cars were not permitted through this
barricade.
The Barricade on Edinburgh Road near Great
Western Road was opened on 6/12/40 A.M., permitting
Foreign and Chinese pedestrians and traffic to pass
North along Edinburgh Road as far as but not through
the barricade just south of Yu Yuen Road, which
remained closed.
Police patrols were permitted to proceed in
both directions on Yu Yuen Road via Tifeng Road
pages.zh:
静安寺巡捕房，
1940年12月6日。

西区日军路障

1940年12月6日，西区道路封锁区内的局势保持不变。上海西郊市民公共汽车公司的3辆机动巴士于1940年12月6日上午7时开始在与前一日相同的线路上运营，未增派额外巴士投入运营。然而，外国人即使声明打算乘坐这些巴士，也被拒绝通过愚园路东端和海格路的路障。

警务巡逻队获准沿大西路向西行进，并通过大西路与爱丁堡路交叉口的路障，但不允许沿相反方向通过该路障返回。

经搜查后，乘坐私人机动车和银色出租车的中国人被允许自由通过这一特定路障，但步行或乘坐机动车的外国人不得通过此路障。

靠近大西路的爱丁堡路路障于1940年12月6日上午开放，允许外国人和中国行人及车辆沿爱丁堡路向北通行，直至但不包括愚园路以南刚刚关闭的路障。

警务巡逻队获准经由地丰路在愚园路上双向通行

pages.en:
- 2 -

and through the barricades on Yu Yuen Road East of
Edinburgh Road.
    Chinese in Private m/cars and Silver Taxis were
permitted freely through this barricade without search
but Foreigners in m/cars were not permitted to pass
although a few Foreigners on foot were permitted to
pass through occasionally.
    At 11 a.m. 6/12/40, three members of S.C.G.P.
Bureau on a m/cycle visited the Tifeng Road Camp
and asked C.P.S. 199, who was on duty inside, how
many police were on duty there and if they were armed.
    At about 1 p.m. 6/12/40, two m/cars, one owned by
the Japanese Military, containing one Japanese Gendarme
in uniform and about 11 other Chinese or Japanese, all
carrying Mauser pistols in their hands, stopped at the
Tifeng Road Camp and demanded that C.P.S. 199 open the
door for them to enter.
    When the C.P.S. replied that he was locked in the
Camp and the keys of the gates were at B'Well Station,
the men tried the gate and then drove away in their
m/car.
    Inspector Yamaguchi made enquiries at 94 Jessfield
Road, but was unable to obtain any information regarding
the reason for this visit to the camp and he was inform-
ed that the men were probably a passing patrol who tried
to enter and inspect the camp.
    At 1 p.m. 6/12/40, three members of the S.C.G.P.
Bureau, one in plain clothes, called at the Public
pages.zh:
- 2 -

并穿过爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）以东愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）上的路障。

FURTHER No. 5. December 6th., 40.
Japanese Military Barricades in the Western District.

S.I. Wilcox.

Sir,
The situation in the Blockaded Area on the
Western District Roads remained unchanged on 6/12/40.
The 3 Buses of the Western Shanghai Citizens
Bus Company commenced operating on the same Routes
as the previous day at 7a.m. 6/12/40, and no
additional Buses have been put into operation.
Foreigners however were refused permission to
pass the Barricades at East End of Yu Yuen Road and Bubbling
Well Road, even though they stated their intention of
proceeding by these Buses.
Police patrols were permitted to proceed west
on Great Western Road and through the Barricade at
Great Western - Minburgh corner but not permitted
to return through the barricade in the opposite
direction.
Chinese in private m/cars and Silver Taxis
were permitted freely through this particular
Barricade after searching, but Foreigners on foot
or in m/cars were not permitted through this
barricade.
The Barricade on Minburgh Road near Great
Western Road was opened at 6/12/40 A.M., permitting
Foreign and Chinese pedestrians and traffic to pass
North along Minburgh Road as far as but not through
the barricade just south of Yu Yuen Road, which
remained closed.
Police patrols were permitted to proceed in
both directions on Yu Yuen Road via Minburgh Road

西区日军路障。

S.I. 威尔科克斯 (Wilcox)。

先生，
1940年12月6日，西区道路封锁区内的局势保持不变。
上海西部市民公共汽车公司的3辆公共汽车于1940年12月6日上午7时开始按前一日的相同路线运营，未增加投入运营的公共汽车数量。
然而，外国人即使声明打算乘坐这些公共汽车，也被拒绝通过愚园路东端和静安寺路的路障。
警队巡逻车获准沿大西路向西行驶，并通过大西路与敏体尼路（Minburgh Road）转角处的路障，但不允许沿相反方向通过该路障返回。
乘坐私人机动车和银色出租车的中国人经搜查后获准自由通过这一特定路障，但步行或乘坐机动车的外国人不得通过此路障。
靠近大西路的敏体尼路（Minburgh Road）上的路障于1940年12月6日上午开放，允许外国人和中国行人及车辆沿敏体尼路向北通行，直至但不包括穿过位于愚园路以南的路障，该路障仍处于关闭状态。
警队巡逻车获准经由敏体尼路在愚园路上双向通行

Japanese Military Barricades in the Western District.

S.I. Wilcox.

Sir,

The situation in the Blockaded Area on the Western
District Roads remained unchanged on 6/12/40.

The 3 M/Buses of the Western Shanghai Citizens
Bus Company commenced operating on the same Routes
as the previous day at 7 a.m. 6/12/40, and no
additional Buses have been put into operation.

Foreigners however were refused permission to
pass the Barricades at East End of Yu Yuen and B'Well
Roads, even though they stated their intention of
proceeding by these Buses.

Police patrols were permitted to proceed west
on Great Western Road and through the Barricade at
Great Western - Edinburgh corner but not permitted
to return through the barricade in the opposite
direction.

Chinese in private m/cars and Silver Taxis
were permitted freely through this particular
Barricade after searching, but foreigners on foot
or in m/cars were not permitted through this
barricade.

The Barricade on Edinburgh Road near Great
Western Road was opened on 6/12/40 a.m., permitting
Foreign and Chinese pedestrians and traffic to pass
North along Edinburgh Road as far as but not through
the barricade just south of Yu Yuen Road, which
remained closed.

Police patrols were permitted to proceed in
both directions on Yu Yuen Road via Tifeng Road

西区日军路障。

S.I. Wilcox。

先生：

1940年12月6日，西区道路封锁区内的局势保持不变。

上海西部市民公共汽车公司的3辆机动巴士于1940年12月6日上午7时开始运营，路线与前一日相同，且未增派额外巴士投入运营。

然而，外国人即使声明打算乘坐这些巴士，也被拒绝通过愚园路和静安寺路东端的路障。

警队巡逻车获准沿大西路向西行驶，并通过大西路与爱丁堡路交叉口的路障，但不允许沿相反方向通过该路障返回。

乘坐私人机动车和银色出租车的华人在接受搜查后，可自由通过这一特定路障，但步行或乘坐机动车的外国人则不允许通过此路障。

靠近大西路的爱丁堡路路障于1940年12月6日上午开放，允许外国和华人行人及车辆沿爱丁堡路向北通行，直至但不得通过位于愚园路以南的路障，该路障仍处于关闭状态。

警队巡逻车获准经由提丰路（Tifeng Road）（音译）在愚园路上双向行驶

carrying Mauser pistols in their hands, stopped at the
Tifeng Road Camp and demanded that C.P.S. 199 open the

When the C.P.S. replied that he was locked in the

the men tried the gate and then drove away in their

Inspector Yamaguchi made enquiries at 94 Jessfield
Road, but was unable to obtain any information regarding
the reason for this visit to the camp and he was informed
that the men were probably a passing patrol who tried
to enter and inspect the camp.

1940年12月6日下午1时许，两辆机动车（其中一辆为日本军方所有）载有一名身着制服的日本宪兵及约11名其他中国人或日本人，所有人手中均持有毛瑟手枪，在提篮桥路营地停下，并要求巡捕199号开门让他们进入。

位于愚园路的女子学校，并向门口的身穿便衣的华籍警员（C.P.W.）查询在该处受雇的所有更夫的详情。离开前，他们嘱咐该便衣华警请该校校长于1940年12月6日下午2时前往极司菲尔路13号出席会议。

该校校长亚历山大小姐（Miss Alexander）从学校窗口看到这些人与便衣华警交谈，随后她致电警司贝斯特（Best），报告了此事，并表示她将不出席该会议。

1940年12月4日下午2时，署名人与许警司（Inspector Hsu）前往极司菲尔路13号，会见了上海特别市警察局（S.C.G.P.Bureau）的王道尊警司（Inspector Wang Tao Tsun (音译)），后者称，根据上海特别市警察局的命令，拟撤换封锁区内受雇的所有更夫，无论是私人雇佣的还是警察系统的，并改由上海特别市警察局提供的更夫接替。

外国人及其他希望保留现有更夫的雇主，上海特别市警察局或许会允许其继续留用，但前提是雇主需提供担保人，且更夫须穿着上海特别市警察局的制服并接受其管辖。

向王警司解释说，这些学校和营地属于工部局（S.M.C.）财产，其更夫由工部局警务处（S.M.P.）和志愿后备队（V.S.D.）提供。

他回答说，如果工部局有任何异议，应向上海特别市警察局提出交涉。

1940年12月6日晚9时，居住于爱文义路506号的英格利斯（Inglis）先生致电警局报告称，居住在忆丰路4弄3号的英国人T.J.史密斯（T.J. Smith）先生在大西路与爱丁堡路路障处被特别市政府警察逮捕。

巡警822号致电极司菲尔路94号，查明史密斯先生是因在路障处发生轻微误会而被捕。

1940年12月6日晚9时30分，又收到英格利斯先生的电话消息，称史密斯先生已被释放，当时正与其一同待在法租界一位朋友家中。据信当时处于醉酒状态的史密斯先生拒绝在电话中交谈，并表示他将于1940年12月6日上午前往静安寺警局报案。

1940年12月6日上午8时45分，史密斯先生来到静安寺警局报案称，1940年12月6日午夜左右，在爱丁堡路-大西路路障处，他被拒绝通过路障，在随后发生的争执中，他殴打了一名英国巡捕，随后被要求前往警局

He did not wish to take the matter any further and

He was unable to give a better description of the

House to house searches by the Japanese Gendarmerie
were continuing throughout the day in the blockaded area
bordered by Great Western, Edinburgh and Yu Yuen Roads.

No reports of undue hardships through lack of food,
etc., were received or noticed in the area and discreet
enquiries reveal that most of the residents have removed,
but those remaining in area where lines are barricaded
are assisted in obtaining food supplies and daily
necessities by members of the S.M.P. Bureau, who are
on duty in vicinity.

Japanese Military Barriers in the Western District.

S. I. Wilcox.
Officer i/c District. C.I.

Sir,

On 5-1-40, there were signs of improvement in the situation regarding Western Area Roads.

At 8 a.m. 5-1-40, the Japanese Gendarmerie would not permit C. M.C. Traffic Guards to be posted at B'well and Tifang Roads corner. They were however again posted at that point between 8 p.m. and 12 p.m.

At 10.30 a.m. Chief Inspector West on patrol was stopped and not permitted to proceed west through the Yu Yuen - Edinburgh Road barricade.

The posters pertaining to Major Hunt were removed from the Barricades at 12 noon and shortly afterwards were replaced at all Barricades by printed notices in Chinese which reads as follows:-

"Residents in the blockaded area can gain access by passing through Yu Yuen - Edinburgh Roads, Great Western - Edinburgh Roads, or the Soe Ka Hong Villages.
Private m/cars, Silver Taxis and Public m/buses for the Western Area are the only vehicles allowed to pass".

Chopped:- Japanese Gendarmerie.
S.C.S.P.D.

On 5-12-40, the Western Shanghai Citizens Bus Company commenced operating a m/bus service on Yu Yuen Road between Yu Yuen Road - Settlement Boundary Barricade to D. C. (Divisions) and Jessfield Park at a Flat Rate of 20 cents per trip with one stopping place en route at Edinburgh Road corner

Although Foreigners were permitted to board these buses at the starting point, they were compelled to alight at Yu Yuen - Edinburgh Roads corner and were not permitted to pass through the Barricade at that point either

西区日军路障。

S. I. Wilcox。
辖区主管警官。刑事侦缉处。

先生：

1940 年 1 月 5 日，西区道路局势出现好转迹象。

1940 年 1 月 5 日上午 8 时，日本宪兵不允许工部局交通警在静安寺路与提篮桥路（音译）转角处执勤。然而，在晚上 8 时至 12 时之间，他们再次被派往该地点执勤。

上午 10 时 30 分，巡官 West 在巡逻时被拦下，不被允许穿过愚园路—爱丁堡路路障向西行进。

中午 12 时，有关 Hunt 少校的海报从路障上被移除，不久之后，所有路障处均换上了中文印刷告示，内容如下：-

“封锁区内居民可通过愚园路—爱丁堡路、大西路—爱丁堡路或曹家巷（音译）村庄进入。
仅限私人摩托车、银色出租车及西区公共公共汽车通行”。

盖章：- 日本宪兵队。
S.C.S.P.D.

1940 年 12 月 5 日，上海西区市民巴士公司开始在愚园路上运营公共汽车服务，路线从愚园路—租界边界路障至 D. C.（分区）和极司菲尔公园，单程统一票价为 20 分，途中在爱丁堡路转角设有一个停靠站。

虽然外国人获准在起点登上这些巴士，但他们被迫在愚园路—爱丁堡路转角下车，且不被允许通过该处的路障。

第2页

乘公共汽车或步行。

该路线的服务由两辆公共汽车开始运营，牌照号码为 20042 和 20043。第一辆载有中国乘客的公共汽车于 1940 年 12 月 5 日下午 3 时 45 分从豫园路东关卡出发，由一名骑摩托车的日本宪兵护送。

大约在同一时间，另一辆属于同一家公司的公共汽车（牌照号码 20041）从倍开尔路（B'Well Road）福特租车行西侧的关卡开始运营，经由大西路（Gt. Western Road）和哥伦比亚路（Columbia Road）行驶至阿美士德路（Amherst Avenue）与哥伦比亚路转角处，收取相同车费，并在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）转角东侧设有一个停靠站。

在终点站雇用了中国稽查员，并在阿美士德路与哥伦比亚路转角处的一家小香烟店内设立了一间办公室，同时在大西路与爱丁堡路转角处的停靠站附近正在安装另一间办公室。

据其中一名稽查员查明，该公司仅有这三辆机动公共汽车，其所有者名为潘三商（Pan Sai San），此人与经营 O.O.L. 的赌窟有关联，并为其颁发执照。

他居住在金西尔路（Kinsear Road），并在该处设有办公室。

这三辆公共汽车于 1940 年 12 月 15 日晚上 8 时 40 分停止当日运营，随后停放在位于金西尔路的车主住所过夜。

另注意到，意图乘坐这些机动公共汽车的中国人被允许通过关卡

It should be mentioned however that the position of
the Barricades in the District are continually being
changed without notice and the different parties of
Japanese Gendarmes on duty use their own discretion as to

Information was also obtained to the effect that the
various Consular Authorities would be issued passes for

另据信，每次乘车会发放不同颜色的车票，乘客下车时车票被撕成两半，乘客保留其中一半，凭此半张车票可通过路障。

中国行人似乎可自由通过路障，但外国人不得通过位于爱丁堡路以东的愚园路路障，以及位于爱丁堡路以东的圣西路（St. Western Road）路障。

上海公共租界工部局警务处巡逻队允许向西通过这些路障，但不得向东通行。

Sir;

An inquest was held over the body of Siau Tsung
Yus (蕭正裕) at the Polo Mortuary on December 2nd,
when, after hearing evidence, Prosecutor Soong Kang
San handed down the following verdict:

"Death due to stray bullet wounds. Body to be
removed by deceased's son Siau Hyung Siau".

The situation on Western Roads are slightly
improved. Foreign traffic pedestrian and owner driven
cars are allowed along Great Western and Yu Yuen Roads
as far as Edinburgh Road via Great Western Road or
Avenue Haig to North along Tifeng Road. It has been
ascertained that a few foreigners have been searched
by members of the S.C.G. Police on barriers. To
travel West of Edinburgh Road is as before; via Avenue
Haig or Jessfield Road.

and D.S. were made copies of small posters posted on

"NOTICE

The complaint of Major Hunt, Military
Attache to British Consulate General are
read as follows:-

By request of the gasoline firm. Are
these loop-ways established in front of the
Japanese Gendarmerie?

People who have still intentions like

Bubbling Well REGISTRY
2nd December 40.

Murder of Japanese Gendarmerie.
Murder of Hsu Tsung Yue on Great Western Road.
Det. Inspector Liddell
C/Inspector i/c.

Sir;

The body of Hsu Tsung Yue (蕭王裕) was removed
from St. Luke's Hospital No.2 on the afternoon of
December 1st, to the Public Mortuary, Ssoochow Road,
pending inquest held on December 2nd.

The Japanese Gendarmerie Lance Corporal Mitsuhei
Yasage who had first aid treatment at the Country
Hospital immediately after the shooting affray was
removed at 7.45 p.m. 1st. to the Japanese Military Hospital,
Singkuo Road, but was dead on arrival.

A complete blockade was put on at about 3 p.m.
December 1st and has if anything been tightened up
since as the kniferest barriers have been reinforced
with barbed wire during the afternoon of December 2nd
and at Bubbling Well - Tifeng Roads corner at least one

Attempted Murder of Japanese Gendarme
Murder of Siau Tsung Yue (蕭正福) on Great Western Road.
D. I. McCahey
S. Mees Officer i/c District. C.I.

Sir,

At 2.25 p.m. a telephone message from C.P.C. 2021
reported a shooting affray on Great Western Road near
Lane 52 A.

Station alarm was sounded and a large party of
Police turned out under Officer i/c when it was ascertai-
ned members of the Japanese Gendarmerie had been fired
upon and they returned the fire.

A call was put into the Reserve Unit which turned
out under Inspector Campbell.

Barrier duties on Settlement Boundary were doubled.

Investigations ascertained that two members of the
Japanese Gendarmerie were proceeding from East to West
along the North footpath of Great Western Road at about
2.20 p.m. When passing Lane 52 A (Wang Ka Loong 汪家弄)
an unidentified gunman emerged from the Lane and opened
fire on the soldiers seriously wounding Lance Corporal
Mitsuhei Onaga. The wounded man fell into the doorway
of a small shop No. I 471 Great Western Road which is on
the West corner of Lane 52 A. No blood stains are
visible, but vomit is visible inside the doorstep.

The uninjured Gendarme swung round and apparently
sighted the criminal take cover round the corner of the
Lane. The soldier, Lance Corporal Hito, ran East about
twelve yards and apparently took cover in a doorway of
House 50 Great Western Road and being armed with a rifle
exchanged shots with the assassin. One rifle shot having
struck the pillar of a gate at the rear of shop I. 471

日本宪兵遇刺案
大西路萧正福（Siau Tsung Yue）被杀案。
分区督察麦卡希（McCahey）
辖区负责人、刑事侦缉警司米斯（S. Mees）

先生：

下午2时25分，中央捕房电话2021打来报告，称在大西路近52A弄附近发生枪击冲突。

警局发出警报，大批警员在辖区负责人带领下出动，经查实系日本宪兵队成员遭人射击，并予以还击。

随即呼叫后备队，该队在坎贝尔（Campbell）巡官带领下出动。

租界边界的路障警戒任务加倍部署。

经调查查明，下午2时20分左右，两名日本宪兵队成员正沿大西路北侧人行道由东向西行进。当经过52A弄（汪家弄）时，一名身份不明的持枪歹徒从弄堂内走出，向士兵开火，致使下士小野光平（Mitsuhei Onaga）受重伤。伤者倒在大西路1471号一家小店铺的门口，该店位于52A弄的西角。现场未见血迹，但门槛内可见呕吐物。

未受伤的宪兵转身，似乎瞥见罪犯躲入弄堂拐角处。该士兵，下士Hito（音译），向东跑了约十二码，似乎躲入大西路50号的门洞内，因配有步枪，遂与刺客互射。其中一发步枪子弹击中了1471号店铺后方一根门柱。

（印：特别处登记室索引归档 日期 1940年12月3日）

Whilst one of the assassins shots struck the pillar
of the doorway in which the soldier took cover. Both
shots however, struck about eighteen inches from the
ground. It may be mentioned that the Eastern corner
of Lane 524 is cut off at an angle whilst the West
corner is square.

On the West corner of Lane 524 an open shoe-
repairer's stall is situated and at the time of the
shooting was occupied by father and son Siau Tsung Yue
(蕭正裕), 68, Kompo, and Siau Myung Siau (蕭銀小),
35, Kompo respectively, residing in the Wang Ka Loong
(Lane 524). During the exchange of shots Siau Tsung
Yue (蕭正裕) was shot in the head and was removed by
S.J.B. Ambulance to St. Luke's Hospital No.2 where
certificate reading "Brought in dead" was issued.

The injured Japanese Corporal was armed with an
automatic pistol which he apparently fired until it
was empty after being struck down himself. This
accounts for Japanese pistol ammunition empty cases
being found at the scene.

Mr. Elly Widler who was in a garage on the North
side of Great Western Road about forty yards West of
Lane 524 heard the shooting. Emerging to the roadway
he saw that a soldier was seriously wounded. He got
out his car and assisted by the uninjured Japanese
Gendarme removed the wounded Corporal to the Country
Hospital about four hundred yards East. A certificate
issued by Dr. V. Bruce M.D. reads "Nov. 30, 1945.

其中一名刺客的子弹击中了士兵藏身的门口立柱。然而，两发子弹均击中距地面约十八英寸处。需提及的是，524 弄的东角呈斜切状，而西角为直角。

在 524 弄的西角设有一个露天修鞋摊，枪击发生时，该摊位由萧正裕（Siau Tsung Yue），68 岁，广东人，及其子萧银小（Siau Myung Siau），35 岁，广东人占据，二人均居住于王家弄（524 弄）。在交火过程中，萧正裕头部中弹，由圣约翰救护队（S.J.B. Ambulance）送往圣路加第二医院（St. Luke's Hospital No.2），院方出具证明称“送医时已死亡”。

受伤的日本军曹配备有一支自动手枪，据称他在自己中弹倒地后一直射击直至子弹耗尽。这解释了为何在现场发现了日式手枪的空弹壳。

埃利·威德勒（Elly Widler）先生当时位于大西路（Great Western Road）北侧、524 弄以西约四十码处的一间车库内，听到了枪声。他走到路上，发现一名士兵身受重伤。他开出自己的汽车，并在一名未受伤的日本宪兵的协助下，将受伤的军曹送往以东约四百码处的广慈医院（Country Hospital）。V. Bruce 医学博士出具的证明写道：“1945 年 11 月 30 日。

On visiting the scene at 3.40p.m. with Inspt.

Siau Hying Siau (蕭銀小)
Kempo
C.D.S. 163
B'Well Stn. 30/11/40 Clerk Lee.

My name is Siau Hying Siau, age 35, native of Kempo,
married, a cobbler and am residing in a straw hut, Wong
Ka Loong off Great Western Road and keeping a stall at
the entrance of North Wong Ka Loong Great Western Road.
At 2.20 p.m. today, November 30, 1940, whilst working
with my father Siau Cheng Yue, age 80, at the stall, we
saw two or three Japanese Gendarmes proceeding from E to W
on Great Western Road and passed North Wong Ka Loong. We
suddenly heard two shots were fired at the E of Wong Ka
Loong. The Japanese Gendarmes then turned their heads
back and fired with their pistols. During this time,
my father was accidentally wounded by stray bullets. I
then stepped forward and holding of my father. At this
time, the shooting was very heavy, I then ran into North
Wong Ka Loong to avoid the incident. A few minutes later,
the shooting ceased, I came out of the alleyway - East of
Wong Ka Loong and there I saw a Japanese Gendarme wounded
and was lying on the ground. Later I called C.P.O.
E857 convey my father to St. Luke's Hospital, No. 2, where
he was found dead on arrival.
The above is my true statement.

Crossmarked by Siau Hying Siau.
John Carey D.I.
pages.zh:
蕭銀小 (Siau Hying Siau)
金浦 (Kempo)
刑事偵緝處檔案號 163
貝爾路警署，1940年11月30日，李巡官記錄。

本人名蕭銀小，現年35歲，籍貫金浦，已婚，職業為鞋匠，居住於大西路黃家弄的一間草棚內，並在大西路北黃家弄口設攤經營。今日，即1940年11月30日下午2時20分，當我與80歲的父親蕭成悅 (Siau Cheng Yue) 在攤位工作時，我們看見兩三名日本憲兵在大西路上由東向西行進，並經過北黃家弄。我們突然聽到大西路黃家弄以東方向響起兩聲槍響。那些日本憲兵隨即回頭，用手槍開火射擊。在此期間，我的父親不幸被流彈擊中受傷。我隨即上前扶住父親。當時槍聲非常密集，我便跑進北黃家弄以躲避事端。幾分鐘後，槍聲停止，我從弄堂走出——位於黃家弄以東，在那裡我看見一名日本憲兵受傷躺在地上。隨後，我呼叫警員編號 E857 將我的父親送往聖盧克醫院二院，抵達時發現他已經死亡。
以上係本人真實供詞。

由蕭銀小畫押。
約翰·凱里 (John Carey)，偵探督察

Murder of a member of Japanese Military Gendarmerie, S.C.G. .E.
Territory.

D.I. McCahey                                          C.I.
                               Officer i/c District.

Sir,
        At 7.30 p.m. October 18, 1940, information was
received from D.C. "Divisions" to the effect that
Japanese Gendarmerie had cordoned off Yu Yuen Road
section between Tifeng and Edinburgh Roads and were
searching pedestrians and vehicles.
        Parties of Police under Officer i/c turned out
to investigate with result that it was ascertained a
member of the Japanese Gendarmerie had been shot and
wounded whilst walking in Lane 668 (S.C.G.P.B.) Yu Yuen
Road at about 1.40 p.m. (2.40p.m. Japanese time).
        D.O. "B" Division, Mr. Grubb was informed and he
attended Bubbling Well with Det. Supt. Clissold,
D.D.O. "B"., Supt. Tabata and Supt. Yao Chin Zu and
visited all posts operated by the Japanese authorities
and eventually ascertained that Corporal Seiseihi Sato,
25 attached to Western Detachment of the Japanese
Military Gendarmerie was at about 1.40 p.m. (2.40p.m.
Japanese time) on his way from the detachment through
Hoo Ka Zah with outlet to Yu Yuen Road through Lane
No. 668 when about two hundred yards from the road three
male Chinese appeared and opened fire on him with
pistols seriously wounding him in the abdomen with two
or three shots, not giving him time to defend himself.
        The injured man was removed to the Yangtseepoo
Military Hospital in a serious condition (later informati-
on was received to effect he had died).
        Immediately after the shooting the area bounded by
Yu Yuen, Edinburgh, Kiaoear, Josefied and Tifeng Roads

麦卡希（McCahey）警司                                          首席督察
                               辖区负责人

先生：
        1940年10月18日下午7时30分，收到来自“各分区”副巡官的情报，称日本宪兵队已封锁愚园路介于狄更斯路（Tifeng Road）与爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）之间的路段，并正在搜查行人和车辆。
        由辖区负责人率领的几组警察出动调查，结果查明，一名日本宪兵队成员于下午1时40分左右（日本时间下午2时40分）在愚园路668弄（属公共租界工部局警务处辖区）内行走时遭枪击受伤。
        “B”分区警官格鲁布（Grubb）先生获悉此事后，会同克拉索尔德（Clissold）侦探总监、“B”分区副分区警官田畑（Tabata）巡官以及姚金祖（Yao Chin Zu，音译）巡官前往静安寺，走访了日本当局运作的所有岗哨，最终查明：隶属于日本陆军宪兵队西部分遣队的曹长佐藤清平（Seiseihi Sato，音译），25岁，于下午1时40分左右（日本时间下午2时40分）从分遣队出发，途经胡家宅（Hoo Ka Zah，音译），经由668弄出口前往愚园路；在距离大路约两百码处，三名中国男子出现并用左轮手枪向他开火，向其腹部射击两至三枪，致其重伤，使其来不及自卫。
        伤者被送往杨树浦军医院，情况危急（后获知消息，称其已死亡）。
        枪击发生后立即，由愚园路、爱丁堡路、胶州路（Kiaoear，原文拼写有误，应为Kiaochow）、约瑟夫路（Josefied，原文拼写有误，应为Joseph）和狄更斯路所围成的区域

Demoliton of Houses
Continues

Chinese Turned out of
Homes in Wang Ka Loong

The demolition process in Wang
Ka Loong in Great Western Road
where, by order of Japanese authori-
ties, Chinese civilian houses have
been torn down, is still going on.
So far no other reason than the
recent shooting of a Japanese officer
which took place there has been
reported for the destruction of the
houses. No compensation is reported
to have been offered.
The Japanese are doing this in
order to give room for new roads
but several hundred poor people have
had their homes destroyed and are
suffering from exposure, it is said.
Household-removing activities are
reported to be still going on and
"To let" notices are said to have
made their first appearance in the
area, urging people to move to
Nantao. Reports indicate that these
notices have been put up by en-
terprising landlords in the native
city.
Some areas in the troubled district
are open to the public traffic only
between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m. and
Chinese police are said to be continu-
ing carrying out their "Po Cha"
system among the residents there,
requiring mutual guarantees against
bad elements.
pages.zh:
房屋拆除
仍在继续

王家弄居民被逐出家园

在大西路（Great Western Road）王家弄，根据日本当局的命令，中国平民的房屋已被拆毁，目前的拆除工作仍在进行中。据报道，除了近期该地发生的一名日本军官遭枪击事件外，尚未有其他关于拆房原因的报道。亦未闻有提供赔偿的消息。

据说，日方此举旨在为新道路腾出空间，但已有数百贫民的家园被毁，正遭受露宿之苦。据悉，搬迁活动仍在进行，该地区已首次出现“招租”告示，敦促人们迁往南市。报告指出，这些告示是由南市一些富有进取心的房东张贴的。

在动荡地区的部分区域，公众交通仅在上午7时至下午6时之间开放。据说，中国警察仍在当地居民中继续执行“保查”制度，要求居民互相担保，以防不良分子。

pages.en:
DEC 20 1940

Japanese Road
Work Continues

Rain Fails To Halt
Project; Nomura
Funeral Held

The Japanese authorities today were still busy with the construction of the projected highway from Great Western Road to Yu Yuen Road, despite the slight rainfall this morning which slowed down the work.

Similarly, construction was proceeding in the widening of a lane along Thorburn Road where last week a Japanese medical officer Surgeon-Lieutenant Masao Nomura was shot by a gunman who was later reported to have been apprehended by the Japanese Naval Landing Party authorities.

Services Held

Memorial services for the late medical officer, who was shot dead while vaccinating Chinese on Ward Road, near Thorburn Road, were held yesterday afternoon at the Nishi-Honganji Temple, Chapoo Road, at noon yesterday.

The services were attended by high-ranking Japanese officials and prominent Japanese businessmen here. Following the services for Surgeon-Lieutenant Nomura a special service for other war dead of the Japanese Expeditionary Forces in Central China was held at the Nishi-Honganji Temple.

Officials Silent

Meanwhile, today, Japanese naval quarters here continued to maintain silence regarding the Chinese who was reported to have been arrested last week following the slaying of Surgeon-Lieutenant Masao Nomura.

It is learned that the arrest was carried out by the Japanese Naval Landing Party at a small Chinese village on Chining Road, near Thorburn Road, after thorough searches had been conducted in the area for more than 24 hours by the Japanese authorities.
pages.zh:
1940年12月20日

日方修路工程
继续进行

降雨未能阻止
工程进度；野村
葬礼举行

尽管今晨微雨导致施工进度放缓，但日本当局今日仍忙于修建从大西路（Great Western Road）至愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）的规划公路。

同样，在托伯恩路（Thorburn Road）沿线的一条弄堂拓宽工程中，施工也在进行。上周，一名日本军医、海军外科中尉野村正雄（Masao Nomura）在此处被一名枪手射杀，据报该枪手随后被日本海军陆战队当局逮捕。

举行仪式

昨日下午，在乍浦路（Chapoo Road）的西本愿寺（Nishi-Honganji Temple），为这位在托伯恩路附近的华德路（Ward Road）为中国民众接种疫苗时遭枪击身亡的已故军医举行了追悼仪式。（注：原文时间表述有矛盾，先称“昨日下午”，后称“昨日中午”，此处依文直译）

多位日本高官及在沪知名日本商人出席了仪式。在为野村外科中尉举行的仪式之后，西本愿寺还专门为华中派遣军的其他阵亡者举行了特别祭奠仪式。

官方保持沉默

与此同时，日本海军驻沪机构今日继续对有关上周野村正雄外科中尉遇害后据报被捕的中国人的情况保持沉默。

据悉，在日本当局对该地区进行了超过24小时的彻底搜查后，日本海军陆战队在托伯恩路附近济宁路（Chining Road）的一个中国小村庄实施了逮捕。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
SP. BR. REGISTRY
No. 44209
2 / 4

Villagers Turned Out
Of Homes

Pitiful Scenes Follow
Japanese Demand

Heartrending scenes are reported
by the leading Chinese dailies to
have been witnessed as the Japanese
required poor people in houses and
huts in the "Wang Village" in Wang
Ka Loong, Great Western Road to
move out on Wednesday from their
dwellings which will be torn down.
It is said that already about 300
huts have been destroyed, rendering
more than 1,000 persons homeless.
These people were seen moving out
from the place carrying with them
whatever meagre personal belong-
ings they could.
The Japanese are said to have
given a time limit for Chinese re-
sidents in the village to leave. The
place is completely separated from
the outside world by the blockade,
no foodstuffs being allowed to be
transported into the area. The re-
ports do not mention the reason for
the Japanese action but it may be
recalled here that it is the place
where a Japanese in uniform was
recently shot. He was the twelfth
Japanese thus attacked in Japanese-
controlled areas, the thirteenth being
shot very recently in Yangtzepoo
near Ward Road. The assassination
wave has been spreading for about
three months.
It is also reported that many people
were seen on Wednesday moving out
from Chi En Pong in Edinburgh
Road because they simply cannot
live there. The blockade there is not
expected to be lifted for a long
time to come, it is stated.

第 44209 号
2 / 4

村民被逐出家园

日方要求引发悲惨景象

据主要中文日报报道，周三，当日本人要求居住在大西路（Great Western Road）王家弄（Wang Ka Loong）“王村”房屋和棚屋中的贫民搬离即将被拆除的住所时，现场出现了令人心碎的景象。据悉，已有约 300 间棚屋被毁，导致 1,000 多人无家可归。人们目睹这些居民带着他们所能携带的少量个人财物离开该地。

据说，日本人已给该村的中国居民设定了撤离的最后期限。由于封锁，该地与外界完全隔绝，任何食品均不得运入该地区。报道未提及日方采取行动的原因，但在此可以回顾的是，此地近期发生了一名身穿制服的日本人的枪击事件。他是日军控制区内遭受此类袭击的第十二名日本人，第十三名日本人则于最近在靠近华德路（Ward Road）的杨树浦（Yangtzepoo）被枪杀。暗杀浪潮已蔓延约三个月。

另有报道称，周三有人目睹许多人从爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）的济恩坊（Chi En Pong）搬离，因为他们实在无法在那里继续生活。据称，那里的封锁预计在很长一段时间内不会解除。

pages.en:
Japanese Start Work
On 'Sazaki Boulevard

Lane Widened To Make New Street Honoring
Slain Gendarme; 2000 Persons In Area
Hit By Project; Ricshas Licensed

More than 200 Chinese laborers were today busy under
Japanese supervision in the construction of a new thorough-
fare from the center of Great Western Road, where a
Japanese gendarme was shot nearly three weeks ago,
through to Yu Yuen Road.

The existing lane standing in
the "path" of the projected high-
way, known as Wong Kya Loong,
will be widened and extended, it is
learned, while Chinese houses
abutting on the lane will be de-
molished.

Houses Reduced

It was estimated this morning
that about only 20 percent of
the buildings and homes in the
lane will remain here after the
completion of the new, Japanese-
sponsored thoroughfare.

About 2000 persons living in the
area are expected to be affected
by the project, which is similar to
that carried out nearly two months
ago on Jessfield Road following
the shooting of another Japanese
gendarme which led to a
"blockade" and then the de-
struction of Chinese homes in the
vicinity rendering nearly 4000 per-
sons homeless.

Named After Gendarme

The new thoroughfare leading
from Great Western Road through
to Yu Yuen Road will be named
after Private Sazaki who was shot
nearly three weeks ago, pre-
cipitating drastic restrictions in
the area by the Japanese and a
severe blockade which virtually
cut off the district from the rest
of the city.

Meanwhile, following the re-
moval of most of the restrictions
in the area last Saturday, the
Chinese municipality announced
that ricshas in the western district
would be required to obtain
Shanghai Special Municipality
licenses.

S.M.C. Protest

While this regulation is being
enforced at present in the western
"outside roads" area by the Chin-
ese authorities, the Shanghai
Municipal Council this week
protested on the matter to the
Japanese Consulate here and is
understood to be taking up the
question with the Chinese muni-
cipality.

Through this latest action on the
part of the Shanghai Special
Municipality, it was learned from
one source this morning, the Chin-
ese authorities hope to be able to
obtain an additional revenue of
about $200,000 a year.

Meantime, however, the Chinese
municipality has indicated that its
latest decree will only affect ricshas
and all other vehicles will be per-
mitted to pass through in the area
as before.
pages.zh:
日方开工修建
“佐崎大道”

拓宽弄堂以新建街道纪念遇害宪兵；该地区2000人受工程影响；人力车须领执照

今天，200多名中国劳工在日方监督下忙碌施工，修建一条从大西路（Great Western Road）中心延伸至愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）的新干道。近三周前，一名日本宪兵正是在大西路中心处遭枪击。

据悉，位于规划干道“路径”上的现有弄堂——名为王家弄（Wong Kya Loong，音译）——将被拓宽和延伸，而紧邻该弄堂的中国民房将被拆除。

房屋减少

今晨估计，在这条由日方主导的新干道完工后，该弄堂内仅约20%的建筑和住宅得以保留。

预计居住在该地区的约2000人将受到该项目的影响。此项目与近两个月前在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）实施的行动类似，当时另一名日本宪兵遭枪击，导致该地区被“封锁”，随后附近的中国民房被毁，致使近4000人无家可归。

以宪兵命名

这条从大西路通往愚园路的新干道将以佐崎二等兵（Private Sazaki，音译）的名字命名。佐崎于近三周前遭枪击，此事促使日方在该地区实施严厉限制及严密封锁，实际上切断了该区与城市其他部分的联系。

与此同时，随着上周六该地区大部分限制措施的解除，中国市政府宣布，西区的人力车须领取上海特别市政府执照。

工部局抗议

虽然中国当局目前正在西区“越界筑路”区域执行这一规定，但上海公共租界工部局本周就此向日驻沪领事馆提出抗议，并据悉正与中国市政府交涉此事。

据今晨消息来源称，通过上海特别市政府的这一最新举措，中国当局希望每年能额外获得约20万美元的收入。

然而，与此同时，中国市政府已表示，其最新法令仅影响人力车，所有其他车辆仍将像以前一样允许通过该地区。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
SP. BR. REGISTRY
N. 424
/ /

WESTERN DISTRICT
CONDITIONS EASY

Searches Conducted On
Settlement Buses
Within Area

With the lifting of the blockade
in the Western District, by the
Japanese authorities on Friday, con-
ditions within the area have become
definitely easier. However, searches
were still being conducted yester-
day upon Chinese travelling on the
number one bus route on Yu Yuen
Road, by members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie and of the City Gov-
ernment Police.

Only eight vehicles of the China
General Omnibus Company were
operating along Yu Yuen Road, yes-
terday afternoon and these ran
from Jessfield Park to St. Georges
and return. Conditions were, on the
whole, as near normal as could be
expected. Pedestrians were permit-
ted to pass through the points where
barricades were formerly erected,
without search, questioning or
molestation.

As regards the infringement on
the Council-granted franchises to
the two transportation companies
for operating vehicles along the
Extra-Settlement Roads as well as
the imposition of payment for Chin-
ese licences for rickshas running
within the area in question, Mr.
W. J. Keswick, Chairman of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, has
made protests to the Japanese
Consul-General.

Blockade free

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别科登记处
编号 424
/ /

西区
局势缓和

在区域内
对租界公交车
实施搜查

随着日本当局于周五解除西区的封锁，该区域内的局势已明显趋于缓和。然而，昨日日本宪兵队及市政府警察成员仍在愚园路一号公交线路对中国乘客进行搜查。

昨日下午，仅有八辆中国公共汽车公司的车辆在愚园路运营，往返于兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）与圣乔治堂（St. Georges）之间。总体而言，局势已恢复到尽可能接近正常的状态。行人获准通过此前设置路障的地点，无需接受搜查、盘问或骚扰。

关于侵犯工部局授予两家运输公司在越界筑路路段运营车辆的特权，以及对在该区域行驶的人力车强制征收中国人执照费一事，上海公共租界工部局总董凯瑟克（W. J. Keswick）先生已向日本总领事提出抗议。

封锁解除

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别科）

pages.en:
Public Nervous
Buses Resume
Normal Runs
In W. District

With the resumption of normal bus and tram transportation, conditions in the western district yesterday had practically returned to normal.

Only a small section of Edinburgh Road was still barricaded. Motorists and pedestrians going north from Avenue Haig found barricades on the south side of the Great Western Road junction.

Pedestrians for a time made use of an alley which runs parallel to Great Western Road northward from Edinburgh Road but when city government discovered the detour, this alley was also barricaded.

An official of the China General Omnibus Company told The China Press that all lines were making their normal runs into the once blockaded area, although the shuttle bus from St. George's to Jessfield was maintained until a late hour in the afternoon.

Although the weather was warm and the sun was bright, visitors at the Jessfield Park were few, apparently due to the fact that residents here have not gotten over their nervousness.

Settlement rickshas, however, were still banned from the district. City government police were seen standing guard at all important street entrances leading from the Settlement and Concession into the western district ordering the vehicles to keep out.
pages.zh:
公众神经紧张
公共汽车恢复
正常运营
于西区

随着公共汽车和有轨电车交通恢复正常，昨日西区的状况已基本回归常态。

仅爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）的一小段仍设有路障。从海格路（Avenue Haig）向北行驶的驾车者和行人，在大西路（Great Western Road） junction 的南侧发现了路障。

行人一度利用一条从爱丁堡路向北、与大西路平行的弄堂绕行，但当市政府发现这条绕道后，该弄堂也被设障封锁。

中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）的一位官员告诉《字林西报》（The China Press），所有线路均已恢复进入曾遭封锁区域的正常运营，尽管从圣乔治教堂（St. George's）到兆丰公园（Jessfield）的接驳巴士一直维持运营至下午很晚的时候。

虽然天气暖和，阳光明媚，但前往兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）的游客寥寥无几，这显然是因为当地居民尚未摆脱紧张情绪。

然而，租界人力车仍被禁止进入该区。有人看到市政府警察在通往西区的所有重要街道入口处站岗，这些入口连接着公共租界和法租界，警察命令车辆不得入内。

pages.en:
Million Dollar
Squeeze Raises
Badland Barrier

Gambling Dens Offer
Funds As “Fine;”
New Road Built

The sum of $1,000,000 was obtained by the Japanese Gendarmerie in the western area from Chinese gambling dens and other “interests” in the district as a “fine” toward lifting the blockade, it was reliably learned this morning.

It is understood that the major part of the “fine” was paid by the China Club gambling house, which reportedly paid $300,000 while the additional amount was “subscribed” to by several other gaming dens and several other public enterprises in the western district.

Japanese Road Building

This morning the Japanese authorities in the area were busily engaged in the construction of a new thoroughfare linking Great Western Road with Yu Yuen Road, the project cutting through from Great Western Road from the spot where Private Sazaki of the Japanese gendarmerie was shot a little over two weeks ago.

High wooden gates, painted white, were being placed this morning at the Great Western Road opening of the new road, and it is believed that a permanent guard of Japanese military or Chinese municipality police will be stationed at this point.

Named For Soldier

The new road when completed will be named after Private Sazaki, it is learned, and will be about 40 feet wide. It will be linked to a new thoroughfare which the Japanese are planning from Jessfield Road, where nearly two months ago Corporal Sato was shot.

The latter roadway will be named Corporal Sato and will lead from the Japanese gendarme headquarters at 94 Jessfield Road, around Kinnear Road, and through to Yu Yuen Road, between Tifeng and Edinburgh Roads.

Houses Torn Down

A large number of Chinese houses in the vicinity of Jessfield Road have already been torn down to enable the construction of the road to be named after Corporal Sato. Most of the tenants were forced to quit their homes immediately after the shooting of the Japanese soldier and the imposition of a severe blockade by the Japanese authorities which brought suffering to more than 4000 Chinese for about five days.

It is believed likely that similar steps will be taken by the Japanese authorities in order to construct the highway from Great Western Road to Yu Yuen Road.
pages.zh:
百万美元
勒索抬高
不良地带屏障

赌场提供
资金作为“罚款”；
新建道路

据今晨可靠消息，日本宪兵队在该西区从华人的赌场及其他当地“利益方”处索取了100万美元，作为解除封锁的“罚款”。

据悉，这笔“罚款”的大部分由“中国总会”（China Club）赌场支付，据报道其支付了30万美元，其余款项则由西区其他几家赌场及若干公共企业“认捐”。

日军修路

今晨，该地区的日本当局正忙于修建一条连接大西路（Great Western Road）与愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）的新干道，该工程从大西路切入，起点位于两周多前日本宪兵佐崎（Sazaki）二等兵被枪击之处。

今晨，在新道路的大西路入口处，正在安装漆成白色的高大木门，据信此处将驻扎日本军队或中国市政警察的常设警卫。

以士兵命名

据悉，这条新路完工后将命名为佐崎二等兵路，路宽约40英尺。它将与另一条日本方面计划修建的新干道相连，后者起自极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road），近两个月前佐藤（Sato）下士在此处被枪击。

后一条道路将命名为佐藤下士路，从位于极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队总部出发，绕过金尼尔路（Kinnear Road），直通愚园路，介于地丰路（Tifeng Road）与爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）之间。

房屋被拆

为修建将以佐藤下士命名的道路，极司菲尔路附近的大量华人房屋已被拆除。大多数租户在日本士兵被枪击以及日本当局实施严厉封锁后立即被迫离开家园，该封锁给4000多名中国人带来了约五天的苦难。

据信，日本当局很可能采取类似措施，以修建从大西路至愚园路的公路。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. BR. REGISTRY
N. 442 (3)
16/ 2/ 45

Two-week Old Western Area
Blockade Lifted Yesterday

Buses, Trams Allowed to Run in Yu Yuen Road
Following the Removal of Barricades

ONE of the longest blockades, imposed by the Japanese authorities on any district in Shanghai, ended yesterday at about noon when all the barriers in Great Western, Yu Yuen and Tifeng Roads were removed, allowing free traffic in the Western Area for the first time in exactly two weeks.

The removal of the barricades saw vehicles of the China General Omnibus Company and trolley buses of the Shanghai Tramways operate in Yu Yuen Road and Amherst Avenue. The Japanese buses, which ran in the restricted area, have been taken off.

It was believed yesterday that other barriers placed by the Japanese authorities and members of the Shanghai Special Municipality Police would be removed in the near future. Some of these had been placed in Singapore, Connaught, Kiaochow and other boundary roads just a few days ago.

Although there is no official confirmation, it is believed that the Japanese authorities have arrested several suspects. The very first day of the blockade, on November 30, the Japanese arrested nine Chinese, while, one Russian of poor class was also detained by them. These arrests were all effected in Great Western Road, just a few steps from the spot where the unidentified gunman shot the Japanese gendarme.

That the blockade would be lifted in the very near future was predicted by the Japanese Embassy spokesman, who added that the barricades would be removed as soon as the Japanese authorities would end their investigations.

The restrictions were slightly relaxed on Thursday evening when the Japanese authorities removed the barriers in Great Western Road and lifted the curfew.

The blockade, the longest ever suffered by this city, started shortly after 2 p.m. on November 30 when Private Sazaki of the Japanese Gendarmerie was shot by a Chinese gunman just outside Lane 52 in Great Western Road. The other Japanese gendarme, in whose company the victim was at the time of the shooting, attempted to bring the culprit down and fired several shots at him, none of which had taken any effect. The wounded gendarme was taken to the Country Hospital, but was later removed by the Japanese to Hongkew. On the way there, he died. Dr. D. W. Nance, who treated the wounded gendarme when he was brought to the hospital, stated that an operation would have saved his life if it had been performed on the spot.

Following the shooting of Sazaki, the Japanese closed all the entrances into the area, not allowing even foreigners to pass through. The conditions in the district became serious as a shortage of foodstuffs began to be felt. The severe restrictions imposed by them hit all the residents in the area, foreigners being inconvenienced in a big way, school children and teachers finding themselves in difficulties on several occasions, while five foreign women and eighty Chinese operators were stranded in the Lucerne Exchange in Edinburgh Road for several days.

Later, Mr. Poul Scheel, senior consul here, made representations to the Japanese Consul-General, resulting in the relaxation of restrictions in the area, although buses and trams were not allowed to run in Yu Yuen Road. The Japanese, instead, started running their own buses and explained this by stating that they wished to prevent inconvenience to people in the area, and adding that the measure was only a temporary one.

Representations

The China General Omnibus Company and the Shanghai Tramways, nevertheless, protested to the Shanghai Municipal Council, and the latter made representations to the Japanese authorities. No reply, however, had been received by the Council.

Yesterday, the Shanghai Municipal Council made further representations to the Japanese Consul-General over the conditions arising out of the blockade in the Western Area, drawing the attention of the Japanese Consul-General to the interference with watchmen employed in the area and to the irregularity of the requirements that rickshaws operating in the Council's roads must obtain Chinese licences.

The attack on Private Sazaki was the twelfth made on Japanese nationals since September 26 when Major Isebe was mortally wounded while walking in North Szechuen Road. All with the exception of three were carried out in the Hongkew District. One of the assaults took place in the Siccawei Sector while the other two in the Western Area, the first being the assassination of Corporal Sato of the Western Area Gendarmerie.

It was learned yesterday that the gambling houses, some of which had been forced to close up because of the restrictions imposed, would open their doors this evening.

（批：Blockade / Feir）
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
南区登记处
编号 442 (3)
1945年2月16日

西区封锁两日后于昨日解除

路障移除后，公共汽车与电车获准在愚园路行驶

上海任何地区所遭受的最长一次封锁——由日本当局实施——于昨日中午左右结束，当时大西路、愚园路和地丰路的所有路障均被拆除，使得西区在整整两周后首次恢复交通自由。

随着路障的移除，中国公共汽车公司的车辆以及上海电车的无轨电车开始在愚园路和阿姆斯特赫斯特大道（Amherst Avenue）运营。此前在限制区域内运行的日本公共汽车已撤出。

据信，日本当局和上海特别市警察成员设置的其他路障将在不久的将来被移除。其中一些路障就在几天前才设置在新加坡路（Singapore Road）、康纳路（Connaught Road）、胶州路及其他边界道路上。

虽然尚未得到官方证实，但据信日本当局已逮捕数名嫌疑人。在封锁的第一天，即11月30日，日本人逮捕了九名中国人，同时一名贫困阶层的俄罗斯人也被他们拘留。这些逮捕行动均发生在大西路，距离那名身份不明的枪手射击日本宪兵的地点仅几步之遥。

日本大使馆发言人曾预测封锁将在极短时间内解除，他补充说，一旦日本当局结束调查，路障就会被移除。

周四晚间，限制措施略有放松，当时日本当局拆除了大西路的路障并解除了宵禁。

这次封锁是本市有史以来持续时间最长的一次，始于11月30日下午2点后不久，当时日本宪兵队士兵萨扎基（Sazaki）在大西路52弄外被一名中国枪手射击。事发时与受害者同行的另一名日本宪兵试图制服凶手，并向其开了数枪，但均未击中。受伤的宪兵被送往宏恩医院（Country Hospital），但随后被日本人转移至虹口。在前往虹口的途中，他死亡。当受伤宪兵被送至医院时，为其诊治的 D. W. Nance 医生表示，如果当场进行手术，本可挽救他的生命。

萨扎基遇袭后，日本人关闭了进入该区域的所有入口，甚至不允许外国人通过。由于开始感到食品短缺，该地区的情况变得严峻。他们实施的严厉限制打击了该地区的所有居民，外国人大感不便，学校师生多次陷入困境，而五名外国妇女和八十名中国职员则在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）的卢塞恩交易所（Lucerne Exchange）被困数日。

后来，此地资深领事 Poul Scheel 先生向日本总领事提出交涉，导致该地区的限制措施有所放松，尽管公共汽车和电车仍不被允许在愚园路行驶。作为替代，日本人开始运行他们自己的公共汽车，并解释称此举旨在防止给该地区民众带来不便，同时补充说这一措施只是临时性的。

交涉

尽管如此，中国公共汽车公司和上海电车公司向上海公共租界工部局提出抗议，工部局随即向日本当局提出交涉。然而，工部局未收到任何回复。

昨日，上海公共租界工部局就西区封锁引发的状况向日本总领事进一步提出交涉，提请日本总领事注意对受雇于该地区的更夫进行的干扰，以及要求在上海公共租界工部局道路上运营的人力车必须领取中国执照这一规定的不合理性。

对士兵萨扎基的袭击是自9月26日伊势部（Isebe）少佐在四川北路行走时受重伤以来，针对日本国民发生的第十二起袭击事件。除三起外，所有袭击均发生在虹口区。一起袭击发生在徐家汇区，另外两起发生在西区，其中第一起是西区宪兵队下士佐藤（Sato）被暗杀。

昨日获悉，赌场——其中一些因实施的限制措施而被迫关闭——将于今晚重新开放。

（批注：封锁 / Feir）

pages.en:
Japanese Lift
Blockade Of
Western Area

Buses, Trolleys Resume
Runs Along Yu Yuen,
Great Western Rds.

RESIDENTS RELIEVED;
CONDITIONS NORMAL

Almost two weeks to the
hour after it was imposed, the
blockade of the Western Area
was lifted by the Japanese
authorities shortly before noon
yesterday. With the removal
of the barricades from the
centre of the roads to the pave-
ment and the discontinuance of
searches of pedestrians and
vehicles, both trolleys of the
Shanghai Electric Construction
Company, Limited, and buses
of the China General Omnibus
Company once again resumed
operating along routes granted
to them under the Council
franchise.

Residents of the blockaded area
as well as those residing farther
west gave a sigh of relief when
they saw and heard that the block-
ade had been lifted and that they
would not have to suffer the hard-
ships and inconveniences that they
had to undergo during the past
fortnight.

The situation in the formerly
blockaded area returned to normal
yesterday afternoon with the ex-
ception that numbers of Japanese
gendarmes were still standing along-
side barricades and closely watch-
ing all pedestrians and vehicles.
Neither the Japanese gendarmes
nor the City Government constables
resorted to searching any pedes-
trians or vehicles after the block-
ade was lifted.

Results Unknown

It could not be ascertained yes-
terday whether the Japanese
authorities had been successful dur-
ing the fortnight's blockade and
intensive searches in the blockaded
area to arrest the actual killer or
suspects in connection with the
killing of Private Sazaki of the
Japanese Gendarmerie, on Saturday,
November 30, which precipitated
the blockade.

Protests Made

The Chairman of the Shanghai
Municipal Council, Mr. W. J. Kes-
wick, had early in the week pro-
tested to the Japanese Consul-
General regarding conditions aris-
ing out of the blockade in the
Western Extra-Settlement Area, as
well as the infringement on the
Council-granted franchises to the
two transportation companies for
operating vehicles along Extra-
Settlement Roads.

Yesterday morning, prior to the
lifting of the blockade, the Chair-
man of the Council drew the at-
tention of the Japanese Consul-
General to the interference with
watchmen employed in the blockad-
ed area and to the irregularity of
the requirement that ricshas
operating upon the Council's roads
must obtain Chinese licences.

Official quarters believed yester-
day that now that the blockade
had been lifted, the majority of
the minor irregularities would be
ironed out shortly.

The blockade, which lasted two
weeks, was the most severe to be
imposed by the Japanese author-
ities in the Western area and had
greatly handicapped residents in the
area. Some of the residents, at the
start of the blockade, had been un-
able to return to their homes for
over 48 hours; others, who were
home at the time that the blockade
was started, were unable to leave.
pages.zh:
日方解除
西区封锁

公共汽车、有轨电车恢复
沿愚园路、大西路运行

居民如释重负；
局势恢复正常

在实施封锁将近整整两周后，日本当局于昨日中午前不久解除了对西区的封锁。随着路障从道路中央移至人行道，并停止对行人和车辆的搜查，上海电力建设有限公司（Shanghai Electric Construction Company, Limited）的有轨电车以及中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）的公共汽车，再次按照工部局特许权授予的路线恢复运营。

当看到并听到封锁已解除，且不必再承受过去两周所经历的艰难与不便时，封锁区内的居民以及居住在更西区域的居民都如释重负。

昨日下午，原封锁区的局势恢复正常，例外之处是有大量日本宪兵仍站在路障旁，严密监视所有行人和车辆。封锁解除后，无论是日本宪兵还是市政府警察，均未再对任何行人或车辆进行搜查。

结果不明

昨日尚无法查明，日本当局在为期两周的封锁及对封锁区的密集搜查中，是否成功逮捕了与11月30日（星期六）日本宪兵佐崎（Sazaki）二等兵被杀案有关的实际凶手或嫌疑人，该事件引发了此次封锁。

提出抗议

上海公共租界工部局总董凯斯威克（W. J. Keswick）先生本周初就越界筑路区域因封锁而产生的状况，以及侵犯工部局授予两家运输公司在越界道路上运营车辆的特许权一事，向日本总领事提出抗议。

昨日早晨，在封锁解除之前，工部局总董提请日本总领事注意对受雇于封锁区的巡捕进行的干扰，以及要求在上海工部局道路上运营的人力车必须领取中国执照这一不合常规的规定。

官方人士昨日认为，既然封锁已经解除，大多数轻微的不规范行为不久将得到解决。

这次持续两周的封锁是日本当局在西区实施的最严厉的一次，给该地区居民造成了极大阻碍。部分居民在封锁开始时，超过48小时无法回家；另一些在封锁开始时身处家中的居民，则无法离开。

pages.en:
11683

West Blockade
Ends; Nippon
Buses Vanish

The fortnight-old Japanese
blockade in the western district
was quietly called off a few
minutes before noon yesterday.
Barbed-wire barricades were
taken down. Restrictions on
traffic were dropped. With a
full-throated roar, Settlement
buses lumbered down Yu Yuen
and Great Western Roads again.
No announcements were made by
the Japanese authorities. The
blockade disappeared as quietly and
unobtrusively as the 8 p.m. cur-
few three days ago.

Only two barbed-wire barri-
cades remained in operation fol-
lowing the new development.
One still cut off the southern
stretch of Edinburgh Road from
Great Western Road, and the
other still stopped traffic on
Great Western Road between
the Country Hospital and
Frazer Motors. These were ex-
pected to be taken down in a
day or two.

S.M.C. Uninformed

Meanwhile, the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council, seemingly oblivious
to the lifting of the blockade, is-
sued a statement late yesterday
afternoon to the effect that an-
other protest had been lodged with
the Japanese Consulate-General re-
garding the alleged interference by
Japanese gendarmes with S.M.P.
watchmen in the affected area, and
the "irregularity" of the Japanese
requirement that rickshas operating
in the area must obtain Chinese
licenses.

Despite the lifting of the
blockade, rickshas were still re-
quired to display a Chinese
license before entering all ter-
ritory west of St. George's late
yesterday.

The second Japanese blockade to
be enforced in the western area
in the last two months, it was the
severest since hostilities passed over
Shanghai in 1937. A large section
of the territory west of St. George's
was cut off from the rest of Shang-
hai.

Caused By Shooting

Restrictions were immediately
clamped down after the shooting
of Corporal Sasaki near Tifeng
Road, the twelfth assassination of

a member of the Japanese forces
in Shanghai in the past ten weeks.
As exclusively related to THE CHINA
PRESS by Elly Widler, wanted by
the Shanghai Municipal Police on
a Swiss Consular warrant, the cor-
poral was shot while on duty with
another gendarme.

Promptly taken to the Country
Hospital in Widler's car he died
shortly afterwards. A tight cordon
thrown around the whole sector is
understood to have drawn a num-
ber of suspects into the Japanese
drag-net. The growing number of
suspects was believed to have
reached a sufficient number yes-
terday, and it was reported that
the killer was among the prisoners.

During the past fortnight many
residents of the affected area had
moved out into more centralized
sectors of the International Settle-
ment. Those who had resolved to
stick it through had been forced to
travel long and roundabout routes
between their offices and residences.

Residents Troubled

With barbed wire barricades
shifting every few days, presumably
in keeping with the spirit of the
times prevailing along European
boundaries, residents of the affect-
ed area were yesterday barely
growing accustomed to a new lay-
out of roads planned out by the
Japanese Army when the restric-
tions were dropped. Ever-shifting
barricades had changed places once
again three days ago.

A new set of formerly-deserted,
suburban roads had been arranged
to take the brunt of western dis-
trict traffic. A short, unassuming
stretch of Tifeng Road between
Great Western and Bubbling Well
Roads had turned over night from
a quiet suburban street to a noisy,
teeming thoroughfare—the sole re-
maining link between Shanghai
and its western areas. The once
peaceful air, filled with hooting, toot-
ing and a bedlam of Oriental col-
loquy for the past two days, was
quiet and peaceful again last night.

Meanwhile, no answer had been
received from the Japanese Con-
sulate-General to a protest lodged
by the Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil as a result of the infringement
of franchise rights of Settlement
transportation companies by a new
Japanese bus line instituted as a
"temporary expediency."
pages.zh:
11683

西部封锁
结束；日本
巴士消失

持续两周的日本西区封锁于昨日中午前几分钟悄然解除。铁丝网路障被拆除。交通限制被取消。伴随着引擎的轰鸣声，公共租界的公交车再次隆隆驶过愚园路和大西路。日本当局未发表任何声明。此次封锁如同三天前晚上8点的宵禁一样，悄无声息且毫不引人注目地消失了。

随着事态的新发展，仅剩两处铁丝网路障仍在运作。一处仍切断爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）南段与大西路的连接，另一处仍阻断大西路在乡村医院（Country Hospital）与弗雷泽汽车行（Frazer Motors）之间的交通。预计这些路障将在一两天内拆除。

工部局未获通知

与此同时，上海公共租界工部局似乎对封锁解除一事浑然不觉，于昨日下午晚些时候发表声明，称已就日本宪兵在受影响区域干扰工部局警务处（S.M.P.）巡捕一事，以及日方要求在该区域运营的人力车必须领取中国执照这一“违规”要求，向日本总领事馆提出另一次抗议。

尽管封锁已解除，但截至昨日晚些时候，人力车在进入圣乔治堂（St. George's）以西的所有区域之前，仍被要求展示中国执照。

这是过去两个月内在西区实施的第二次日本封锁，也是自1937年战火波及上海以来最严厉的一次。圣乔治堂以西的大片区域与上海其他地区被隔绝开来。

起因于枪击事件

在佐佐木下士（Corporal Sasaki）于提丰路（Tifeng Road）附近遭枪击后，限制措施立即实施，这是过去十周内第十二名在上海遇刺的日本部队成员。据《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）独家报道，消息来源为埃利·维德勒（Elly Widler，因持有瑞士领事馆签发的逮捕令而被上海公共租界工部局警务处通缉），该名下士是在与另一名宪兵一同执勤时遭枪击的。

他被迅速用维德勒的汽车送往乡村医院，不久后身亡。据悉，对该整个区域实施的严密封锁已将多名嫌疑人纳入日方的搜捕网中。据信，嫌疑人数目至昨日已达到足够规模，且有报道称凶手就在囚犯之中。

在过去两周里，受影响区域的许多居民已搬至国际租界更为中心的区域。那些决定坚持留下的人则被迫在办公室和住所之间绕行漫长而曲折的路线。

居民受扰

随着铁丝网路障每隔几天就变动一次——这大概是顺应了当时欧洲边界流行的风气——受影响区域的居民昨日才刚刚勉强适应由日军规划的新道路布局，限制措施便被取消了。三天前，不断变动的路障再次更换了位置。

一组原先荒废的郊区道路被安排来承担西区交通的主要压力。提丰路介于大西路与静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）之间的一段短而不起眼的路段，一夜之间从安静的郊区街道变成了喧闹、拥挤的交通要道——成为连接上海与其西部地区的唯一剩余通道。过去两天里，空气中充满了喇叭声、汽笛声和各种东方方言的嘈杂声，而昨晚这里又重新恢复了宁静与平和。

与此同时，针对日本新开设的一条作为“临时权宜之计”的日本巴士线路侵犯租界运输公司特许经营权一事，上海公共租界工部局提出的抗议尚未收到日本总领事馆的答复。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
BR. REGISTRY
13 / 2 / 41

Japanese Shift Barricades
As 8 O'clock Curfew Lifted

Quietly and without formal
announcement of any sort the
8 p.m. curfew on the blockaded
western area lying between Yu
Yuen and Great Western Roads
was lifted by the Japanese
authorities yesterday. Barricades
cutting off the long stretch of
Edinburgh Road between these
two main thoroughfares were
taken down yesterday morning.
Seemingly to balance the scales in
the Western area, restrictions that
were lifted in this part of the dis-
trict were clamped down on roads
that surround the previously
blockaded zone.
"The search for the escaped
assassin of a Japanese corporal
has been concluded in this
area," a Japanese sentry told a
representative of THE CHINA
PRESS who visited the scene of
the blockade yesterday after-
noon. "Searches are now being
conducted in other areas," he
went on to explain.

Areas Not Specified

The "other areas" which were
now feeling the brunt of Japanese
militarism were not specified and
were difficult to define from the
new layout of barricades instituted
yesterday. Barbed wire barricades
that had cut off Edinburgh Road
from the rest of Shanghai after 8
p.m. every night for the past 10
days were placed in such a manner
as to cut off a new stretch of
Edinburgh Road (from Great
Western Road to Avenue Haig)
from the rest of the road.
Edinburgh Road north of Yu
Yuen Road was also barricaded off.
Residents of this district who had
been suffering the most stringent
restrictions to date were forced to
travel down Great Western Road
instead of going by the roundabout
route along Avenue Haig.

New Barricades Set Up

On reaching Tifeng Road, how-
ever, a new set of barricades sepa-
rated the town-going resident from
St. George's. A new route through
Tifeng Road had been planned out
by the Japanese authorities, it was
explained.
The new set of barricades in-
stalled in the area yesterday was
not concentrated around any one
district, THE CHINA PRESS representa-
tive discovered. Placed haphazard-
ly and seemingly without a set plan
these barricades did not seem to
cut off any one district from the
rest of Shanghai.
Whereas previously a long stretch
of territory bounded by Edinburgh,
Yu Yuen, Tifeng and Great Western
Roads was completely cut off, the
regulations enforced yesterday only
succeeded in partially isolating
certain districts. Direct com-
munication between these districts
and the rest of Shanghai was im-
possible, but a roundabout road
was left open in nearly every case.

（批：See unit. Blockade plan）

（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE ... BRANCH）
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
英籍人员登记处
1941年2月13日

日军撤除路障
晚八点宵禁解除

昨日，日本当局悄然且未作任何正式公告，解除了位于愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）与大西路（Great Western Road）之间被封锁的西部区域实施的晚8点宵禁。连接这两条主要干道之间长段爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）的路障于昨日上午被拆除。为了在西部区域保持某种平衡，在该地区部分道路解除限制的同时，对环绕此前封锁区域的道路实施了新的管制。“在此区域搜捕刺杀一名日本下士的逃逸刺客的行动已经结束，”一名日本哨兵告诉《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）的一位代表，该代表于昨日下午探访了封锁现场。“搜查工作目前正其他区域进行，”他接着解释道。

未指明具体区域

目前正承受日本军国主义冲击的“其他区域”并未被具体指明，且根据昨日实施的新路障布局也难以界定。过去10天里，每晚8点后便将爱丁堡路与上海其他地区隔绝的铁丝网路障，其设置方式已改为将爱丁堡路的一段新路段（从大西路至海格路/Avenue Haig）与道路的其余部分隔绝。愚园路以北的爱丁堡路路段也被设障封锁。该区居民迄今一直遭受最严格的限制，如今被迫改走大西路，而不再沿海格路绕行。

设置新路障

然而，当抵达地丰路（Tifeng Road）时，一组新路障将进城的居民与圣乔治堂（St. George's）区域隔开。据解释，日本当局已规划出一条经由地丰路的新路线。《字林西报》代表发现，昨日在该地区安装的新路障并非集中在任何一个特定区域。这些路障放置得杂乱无章，似乎没有既定计划，看起来并未将任何一个区域与上海其他地区完全隔绝。此前，由爱丁堡路、愚园路、地丰路和大西路所围成的长长一片地带被完全切断，而昨日执行的法规仅成功地将某些区域部分隔离。这些区域与上海其他地区的直接交通虽已断绝，但在几乎每种情况下都留有一条绕行道路可供通行。

（批注：见单元。封锁计划）

（印章：公共租界警务处……分局）

pages.en:
SMC Notes Grow
Japanese Get
Protest On
Police Assault

Protest on the disarming, assault and detention of five members of the S.M.P. by Japanese gendarmes Sunday evening was lodged with Japanese Consul-General Tateki Horiuchi yesterday by Mr. W. J. Keswick, Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

This was the second protest lodged by the Council with the local Japanese authorities on developments in the blockaded western area. Representations were made Wednesday on the installation of Japanese bus lines on Yu Yuen and Great Western Roads, and another protest was believed pending on the "order" to ricsha pullers in the sector to equip themselves with City Government licenses before Monday.

The Japanese Embassy spokesman said that both the protests already received were being studied. He would make no further comment on the score.

"The arrest of the five S.M.P. men on Edinburgh Road 9 p.m. Sunday sprang from the death of a City Government policeman, who, according to eye-witness reports, leaped on the running board of a moving car to search or arrest the passengers. Shortly afterwards he was found crumpled on the roadway with a bashed skull. It was believed he was pushed off the running board and injured his head in falling.

While he was being removed by a Fire Brigade ambulance to the St. Luke's Hospital, where he died, an S.M.P. party-headed by Sub-Inspector E. Dalatrey and Chief Inspector Shih, arrived on the spot to make enquiries. Just then a unit of Japanese gendarmes also ran up and disarmed the five S.M.P. men. Chief Inspector Shih was reported to have been struck on the face several times.

The men were taken to western district of the gendarmerie at 94 Jessfield Road, and only released at 11.05 p.m. after negotiations between the Japanese and high S.M.P. officials. One Japanese explanation of the incident, offered unofficially, was that the gendarmes were erroneously informed that the City Government policeman had been shot by the S.M.P. men.
pages.zh:
工部局笔记增多
日方就警察遭袭
提出抗议

上海公共租界工部局总董 W. J. 凯斯威克（W. J. Keswick）先生昨日向日本总领事堀内健吉（Tateki Horiuchi）提出抗议，针对的是周日晚间五名上海公共租界巡捕房（S.M.P.）警员被日本宪兵解除武装、殴打及拘留一事。

这是工部局就封锁区西部事态发展向当地日本当局提出的第二次抗议。周三曾就日本在愚园路和大西路开设公交线路一事进行交涉，另据信还有一项抗议正在酝酿中，涉及要求该区域人力车夫在周一前配备市政府执照的“命令”。

日本大使馆发言人表示，已收到的两项抗议均在研究中。他对此未作进一步评论。

“周日晚9点在爱丁堡路逮捕五名上海公共租界巡捕房警员，起因是一名市政府警察死亡。据目击者称，该警察跳上一辆行驶中汽车的踏脚板，意图搜查或逮捕乘客。不久后，人们发现他蜷缩在马路上，头骨碎裂。据信他是从踏脚板上被推下，坠落时头部受伤。

当消防队救护车将其送往圣卢克医院（St. Luke's Hospital）途中（他在该院身亡）时，由副督察 E. 达拉特雷（E. Dalatrey）和总督察石（Shih，音译）率领的一队上海公共租界巡捕房警员抵达现场进行调查。恰在此时，一队日本宪兵也赶到，解除了五名上海公共租界巡捕房警员的武装。据报道，总督察石面部多次遭击打。

这些警员被带至杰斯菲尔德路94号的日本宪兵队西区驻地，经日方与上海公共租界巡捕房高级官员谈判后，于当晚11点05分获释。关于此事件，日方非正式提供的一种解释是，宪兵误获情报，称该名市政府警察是被上海公共租界巡捕房警员开枪射杀的。”

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
Sp. Br. REGISTRY
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE NEWS BRANCH THE PRESS）
（批：Blockade fees）

OFF THE RECORD

Children . . . What Next?
AN eye-witness told OFF THE RECORD yesterday that following the discovery of the anti-Japanese posters in the blockaded area a number of children, around 10 years old, were arrested by Japanese gendarmes and Chinese policemen. The only reason for the arrests given by the Chinese policemen was that the posters, judging from the uncultivated style of the calligraphy, were believed to have been written by youngsters of tender age.
When reports that the children had been arrested reached the unblockaded area in the western district, rumors followed that if the writers of the posters could not be found the Japanese would round up all the children in areas adjoining the lane where the posters were discovered. Thus far, nothing of the kind has yet happened although the hunt for the 'culprits' were still on.

Check & Double Check
Under the usual slogan, "Impartial Not Neutral," a British contemporary came out a few days ago with an editorial asserting—in fact, doubly asserting—that Santi Quaranta had been occupied by the Italians. This was allegedly backed up by "a Greek claim," and "a Reuter report." Said the morning paper:—"The Greek claim from Athens to the effect that Santi Quaranta on the Albanian coast has been occupied by the Italians, is supported by a report carried by Reuters to the effect that the Italians are retreating along the coast...."
Which reminds us that journalistic sabotage has been rampant in Shanghai of late. About a week ago somebody inserted into an advertisement in Wang Ching-wei's paper, the Central China Daily News, a startling remark about Mr. Wang. Wednesday night Evepost Newscaster Sam Titlebaum, broadcasting over the Evepost station, denounced the Evening Post as having yielded to pressure of Tokyo, Berlin, or the entire Axis all at once. Sam's contract, prior to that, had been cancelled.

Employee Bites Employer
Further, on "Fifth" or "Eighth" columns, when employee bites employer—even though only figuratively and over the air—that should be news by a classical definition. But not for our contemporary, the Evepost, and hippo-hided publisher of the same, George Bruce. All English-speaking Shanghai is still talking of Sam Titlebaum's Wednesday night broadcast on the Post's own radio hour, excoriating his employers for allegedly yielding to Tokyo and/or Berlin pressure, but there's not a word in yesterday's Evepost about it. Evidently, Publisher Bruce's attitude is that of Clark Gable in a scene in "Idiot's Delight"—"I shall treat this outburst with the silent contempt that it deserves." Anyway, Gable mentioned the matter; our Mr. Bruce doesn't.
pages.zh:
上海公共租界
特别处登记室
（印：上海工部局警务处新闻科 新闻界）
（批：封锁费）

非公开记录

儿童……接下来会怎样？
一名目击者昨日向“非公开记录”栏目透露，在封锁区内发现反日海报后，数名约十岁的儿童被日本宪兵和中国警察逮捕。中国警察给出的逮捕理由仅有一条：从书法拙劣的风格判断，这些海报被认为是由年幼孩童所写。
当儿童被捕的消息传到西区未封锁地带后，随之产生谣言称，如果找不到海报的作者，日本人将包围并逮捕发现海报的里弄周边地区的所有儿童。迄今为止，此类情况尚未发生，尽管对“肇事者”的搜捕仍在进行。

反复核查
一家英国当代报刊日前以惯用的口号“公正而非中立”为题发表社论，声称——实际上是双重断言——萨兰塔夸兰塔（Santi Quaranta）已被意大利人占领。据称这一说法有“希腊方面的主张”和“路透社报道”为佐证。该晨报称：“来自雅典的希腊方面主张称，阿尔巴尼亚海岸的萨兰塔夸兰塔已被意大利人占领，这一说法得到了路透社一则报道的支持，该报道称意大利人正沿海岸撤退……”
这让我们想起，近期上海的新闻破坏活动十分猖獗。大约一周前，有人在汪精卫的报纸《华中日报》的一则广告中插入了一句关于汪先生的惊人言论。周三晚，《晚报》电台播音员萨姆·蒂特尔鲍姆（Sam Titlebaum）在《晚报》电台广播中谴责《晚报》屈服于东京、柏林或整个轴心国的压力。在此之前，萨姆的合同已被取消。

雇员咬雇主
此外，在“第五”或“第八”版面上，当雇员“咬”雇主时——即使只是比喻意义上且通过广播进行的——按照经典定义，这也应算作新闻。但对于我们的当代报刊《晚报》及其厚脸皮的出版商乔治·布鲁斯（George Bruce）来说并非如此。所有讲英语的上海人仍在谈论萨姆·蒂特尔鲍姆周三晚在《晚报》自有广播时段中的广播，他在广播中严厉斥责雇主 allegedly 屈服于东京和/或柏林的压力，但昨天的《晚报》上对此只字未提。显然，出版商布鲁斯的态度如同克拉克·盖博（Clark Gable）在电影《愚人的喜悦》（Idiot's Delight）某一场景中的表现：“我将以它应得的沉默蔑视来对待这次爆发。”无论如何，盖博还提到了这件事；而我们的布鲁斯先生却没有。

pages.en:
AL PV
REGISTER 683
4. 2.
14 / 4

Restrictions Ease
In Blockade Zone

Entire Barricade May
Be Removed Shortly;
Some Arrests Made

Following predictions made earlier this week by the Shanghai Evening Post, Japanese authorities in the western area today continued to ease restrictions in the "blockade zone" near Edinburgh Road, although a large number of gendarmes continued to patrol the area and conduct searches.

Last night the Japanese gendarmes withdrew barricades lying between Great Western and Yu Yuen Roads, while the former restrictions of an 8 p.m. curfew in the area was also lifted.

Ending Predicted
Official circles this morning declared that it is likely all the restrictions imposed in the area by the Japanese authorities may be removed by tomorrow or some time early next week.

At the same time, however, it could not be ascertained whether the Japanese gendarmes have "completed" their investigations and search for an alleged "nest of terrorists" in an alley off Edinburgh Road.

Arrests Reported
It is believed that a number of arrests have been made, but Japanese official quarters have so far declined to make any statement in this connection.

This morning, adding to the odd situations which have arisen in the blockade zone, the Japanese gendarmes would only permit cars owned by the Silver Taxi Company to proceed along Yu Yuen Road. No reason for the action directed against the other hire car services could be learned.

Japanese-owned buses were still operating today in the area, despite the protest lodged by the S.M.C. earlier this week with the Japanese Consulate in Shanghai, to which the latter has not yet replied.
pages.zh:
AL PV
登记簿 683
4. 2.
14 / 4

封锁区
限制放宽

路障可能即将
全部撤除；
已有数人被捕

继《上海晚邮报》本周早些时候作出的预测之后，日本当局今日继续放宽爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）附近“封锁区”的限制，尽管仍有大量宪兵在该地区巡逻并进行搜查。

昨晚，日本宪兵撤除了位于大西路（Great Western Road）和愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）之间的路障，同时该地区此前实施的晚上8点宵禁限制也被解除。

预计即将结束

今晨，官方人士宣称，日本当局在该地区实施的所有限制可能会在明天或下周初的某个时候全部取消。

然而，与此同时，尚无法确定日本宪兵是否已“完成”对爱丁堡路旁一条小巷中涉嫌“恐怖分子巢穴”的调查和搜查。

据报道有逮捕行动

据信已有数人被捕，但日本官方部门迄今拒绝就此发表任何声明。

今晨，为封锁区内出现的奇特状况又添一笔，日本宪兵仅允许银星出租车公司（Silver Taxi Company）拥有的车辆沿愚园路行驶。针对其他租车服务所采取的这一行动，其原因无从得知。

尽管工部局（S.M.C.）本周早些时候已向日本驻上海领事馆提出抗议，且日方尚未回复，但日资巴士今日仍在该地区运营。

pages.en:
11689

Lifting Of Western
Area Blockade
Rumored Imminent

Semi-official reports persisted yesterday that the blockade of the western area would be lifted in the near future—perhaps within the next two days. Japanese officials maintained complete silence on the matter, however.

Following added relaxation of restrictions Thursday, conditions in the sector continued unchanged yesterday. A fresh odd sidelight in a situation rich with odd sidelights was the refusal of certain Japanese sentries to allow any taxis past the barricades except those of the Silver Garage.
pages.zh:
11689

西区封锁
据传即将解除

昨日，半官方消息持续流传，称西区的封锁将在近期——或许就在未来两天内——解除。然而，日本官员对此事保持完全沉默。

继周四进一步放宽限制后，该区域的情况在昨日继续保持不变。在这一充满奇特插曲的局势中，又出现了一个新的奇特插曲：某些日本哨兵拒绝让除“银库车行”（Silver Garage）以外的任何出租车通过路障。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
4426
12 / 5 /

DEC 1 - 1943

C.G.O.C. Bus Damaged by
Gang in Western Area

About 30 Men Throw Stones, Then Smash All
Windows ; Driver Slightly Injured

TROUBLE suddenly flared up again last night in the extra-
Settlement road area in the western district when a Route
7 bus of the China General Omnibus Company was victimized by
a gang of 30 men, who did not aim at robbery. The bus was
first stoned and its windows were then smashed. The driver was
manhandled and slightly injured.

When the bus was running in
Edinburgh Road, near Avenue Haig,
at about 8.15 p.m. the men rushed
up to it from ambush and began
smashing its windows with iron bars
and wooden sticks, after stoning it.
They escaped before the police could
do anything. During the riot the
driver was injured slightly but no
passengers were hurt.
Informed quarters took a very
serious view of the incident since
the route traversed last night by the
bus is the only one open to the
western district as far as the Settle-
ment bus traffic is concerned since
both Yu Yuen and Great Western
Roads have been blockaded. Settle-
ment authorities have protested
against the running of a Japanese-
managed bus service in the district.
Asked whether or not the riot had
any political motive, authoritative
circles refused to comment merely
answering "please put two and two
together." Officials of the traffic de-
partment of the bus company refused
to give information last night and a
Chinese source reported that two
buses were involved.
The Shanghai Municipal Council
yesterday was awaiting an official
police report regarding the latest
developments in the Western area,
including the erection of the new
barrier by the Japanese authorities
at the intersection of Changping
Road and Yenping Road, preventing
all vehicles from passing.
The Japanese buses continue to
ply their trade on routes formerly
covered by vehicles of the Settle-
ment tram and bus companies, in
which connection representations
were made by the Chairman of the
Municipal Council a few days ago
to the Japanese Consul-General here,
alleging infringement of the fran-
chises of the two Settlement utility
companies.
